title: operator_workset — the merged stage-3 / stage-4 contract
description:
Mission M3.7: 'operator_workset 的定义融合 阶段3 operator_workset 和 阶段4 workset 为一个'. This schema describes `items/codes/workset.yaml`, the one document m4 has to read. Every one of M3.7's seven requirements is a field or a required file here rather than a paragraph somewhere: executable over descriptive (M3.7.1 — every claim about behaviour points at a script that produces it), yaml/json over markdown (M3.7.2 — the per-operator README.md of the stage-3 half becomes `operators/<id>/operator.yaml`, and prose survives only where it states a *reason*), standard tools over bespoke ones (M3.7.3 — `provenance.magpie_row` carries Magpie's own row verbatim rather than a re-derivation), one-click correctness and one-click performance covering every shape to be optimised with at least three (M3.7.4 — `entrypoints` plus `operators[].shapes` minItems 3), shaped like flashinfer-bench (M3.7.5 — `definition` and `workload` are that project's Definition JSON and Workload JSONL, of which `rank0/` in this repository is the worked instance), a KernelForge one-line script layered *over* that base as an add-on (M3.7.6 — the whole `forge` block is generated from `definition` + `workload` and the validator checks it agrees), and one handoff per operator deferred (M3.7.7 — hence `operators` is a list, not one object).

The single most important property, and the reason m4 may take its ground truth strictly from this artefact (M4.3.5): the numbers in `evidence/performance.json` were produced by `run_performance.sh`, and that is the *same script* m4 runs on its candidate. A ratio between them is therefore a ratio between two runs of one instrument, not between two instruments.

workset_id.description: Names the workset, not an operator: one workset carries every candidate operator from one profile of one model on one architecture. e.g. `qwen36-27b.gfx950.decode`.

produced_by.description: Which code built this. Not decoration: when a workset and the package that grades it disagree, the first question is whether they are the same generation.

ground_truth.description: M4.3.5, and it is the mission item that was **reversed** relative to the previous round. m4 is no longer told to distrust the workset's printed numbers; it is told to take them as ground truth, and to **abort** when the premise under which they were measured does not hold. That instruction is only safe because `check_workset_runs` has already re-run these entrypoints on this hardware. The two lists below are what 'the premise' means, spelled as field names of `environment.schema.json#/properties/fixed` so that the comparison is mechanical.

abort_on_mismatch.description: Hardware and parallelism facts. A difference here makes every number in `evidence/` a number about a different machine, so the consumer stops rather than reporting a ratio across two machines. Default and floor: [gpu_arch, gpu_count, tp_size].

warn_on_mismatch.description: Software facts. A different ROCm or a rebuilt image usually moves a kernel a few percent and sometimes moves it a lot; the consumer records the difference and continues. Default: [image_id, rocm, torch].

environment.description: The environment under which `evidence/` was measured, inlined rather than referenced by path. It is the same document as `items/codes/environment.yaml` and `check_environment` grades that copy; this one exists so that a consumer holding only `workset.yaml` can evaluate the two lists above without opening a second file.

entrypoints.description:
M3.7.4 — 必须一键运行的 correctness test 以及 performance test. Whole-workset, every operator, every shape. Both take the same four options and the contract is that **the workset's own baseline and a consumer's candidate go through the same script**:

    ./run_correctness.sh [--operator ID] [--shape CASE_ID] [--impl PATH] [--json OUT]
    ./run_performance.sh [--operator ID] [--shape CASE_ID] [--impl PATH] [--json OUT]

With no `--impl` they exercise the workset's own baseline and reproduce `evidence/`. With `--impl PATH` they exercise a replacement against the same reference, the same shapes and the same protocol. Exit code 0 means every shape passed; non-zero means at least one did not, and the report says which. Neither script may be edited by a consumer — a change to them makes every measurement incomparable with the baseline, which is the whole point of shipping them.

`--shape` narrows to one case and is what makes `check_workset_runs` affordable: that validator does not grade the recorded evidence, it **re-measures at least one shape itself** and checks its own number against the recorded one, so a full re-run would double the workset's GPU cost at every seal. Without a shape selector the cheap version of that check does not exist and the trust chain would rest on a claim about a claim.

Both refuse to run when a field in `ground_truth.abort_on_mismatch` does not match the host they are on. That refusal is a behaviour of the script and not a paragraph a reader has to obey (M3.7.1).

evidence.description:
Where the baseline run's own reports are, and where they were measured. Produced by running `entrypoints` with no `--impl`. `check_workset_runs` re-runs the entrypoints and compares against these; m4's speedup denominator is `performance_report`, filtered to `impl == "baseline"`.

Optional at the schema level and **required by `check_workset_shape`** — a workset may legitimately not have been measured yet at the moment its author validates its shape, and it may never be handed on in that state.

correctness_report.description: Path relative to `items/codes/`, conventionally `evidence/correctness.json`. Validates against `#/$defs/correctness_report`.

performance_report.description: Path relative to `items/codes/`, conventionally `evidence/performance.json`. Validates against `#/$defs/performance_report`.

logs.description: Path to the captured stdout/stderr of the two runs, relative to `items/codes/`.

protocol.description: The measurement protocol both entrypoints use, declared once here so a consumer can quote it without reading the scripts. `groups` >= 5 and `iters_per_group` >= 10 is the floor the previous round measured to be necessary: the round-to-round spread on a steady node is ~2%, and fewer groups than this cannot distinguish a 5% win from it.

operators.description: One entry per candidate operator. A list rather than one object because M3.7.7 — 每个算子一个单独的 handoff — is **deferred**, not rejected: agent_sys has no 'one output slot per element of a runtime list' (`env_mgr/grants.py:340-355`), so one handoff carries them all and this list is where the split will happen when the framework can express it (`todo.md` T3).

excluded.description: Candidates that were considered and are not in `operators`, each with a reason. Present for the same argument `check_identity_resolved` makes with `min_resolve_ratio: 0.0`: what is checked is that uncertainty is *modelled*, not that it is absent. A workset that silently drops the 63%-of-GPU-time collectives is indistinguishable from one that never saw them.

cmd.description: Relative to `items/codes/`, and relative on purpose: `handoff/locality.py` refuses a seal over any absolute path outside its allow-list, and a `/`-leading fragment in a *comment* has refused a complete delivery before.

protected.description: The consumer may not edit this file. KernelForge already treats `--driver` this way; the same rule applies one level up, because a consumer that edits the instrument controls its own result.

timing.description: How one iteration is timed. `*_graph_replay` removes launch overhead and is what the stage-4 half's `graph_harness.py` does; `event` is device events around the call; `wall` is host-side and is only honest for an operator whose runtime dwarfs a launch.

operator_id.description: Also the directory name under `operators/`, so it is constrained to what a path and a shell variable both tolerate.

kernel_id.description: The id `kernel_worklist` gave it, e.g. `k003`. The join back to m3's own earlier artefacts.

device_symbol.description: What the profiler recorded. It is **not** the unit of work: the unit is the framework-level entry function in `edit_target`, because a device symbol is frequently a generated name that appears nowhere in the checkout. A workset whose `device_symbol` cannot be found in the source is normal and is not a defect; `edit_target.resolution_caveats` is where that is said.

op_type.description: flashinfer-bench's `op_type`, and also the subdirectory under `definitions/` and `workloads/`. `gemm`, `moe`, `attention`, `norm`, `softmax`, …

status.description: Carried over from the stage-3 half's `invocation_spec.json`, where it had already been used correctly and non-obviously: a workset with three *stated uncertainties* but every field filled is `complete`, because `missing_fields` is about fields, and a `partial` that names no field hides the uncertainty rather than recording it.

missing_fields.description: Empty iff `status` is `complete`. `check_workset_shape` enforces the biconditional.

definition.description: M3.7.5. A flashinfer-bench **Definition**, byte-shaped like `rank0/definitions/gemm/aiter_gemm_a16w16_nt_n128_k6144.json`: `{name, op_type, axes{var|const}, inputs{shape,dtype}, outputs, reference, baseline, tags, description, constraints}`, where `reference` and `baseline` are Python source strings each ending in `def run(*args, **kwargs)`. That format was not chosen for resemblance — it is the only one in this problem that separates the three things a correctness gate keeps confusing: the *reference* (slow, obviously-right, what correctness is judged against), the *baseline* (the incumbent fast implementation, what speedup is judged against), and the *candidate* (what a consumer supplies).

workload.description: M3.7.5. A flashinfer-bench **Workload** JSONL, one line per shape, each `{definition, workload:{axes, inputs, uuid}, solution: null, evaluation: null}`. **This file is the single source of truth for the shape list**; `shapes` below is a denormalised index of it for validators that should not have to parse JSONL, and `forge.cases` is a generated export. `solution` and `evaluation` are null here by construction: they are the slots a consumer fills, and a workset that pre-fills them is asserting an answer it has not measured.

shapes.description: M3.7.4.1 — 必须提供所有 test case: 包括所有需要优化的形状, 保证在 ≥3. Two requirements, and the second is the weaker one. **Every shape the operator is to be optimised for must appear here**, so a consumer cannot optimise a shape nothing measured; three is the floor at which a performance claim is about an operator rather than about one shape. One row per line of `workload`, in the same order, and `check_workset_shape` checks the correspondence rather than trusting it.

entrypoints.description: The per-operator narrowing of the workset-level entrypoints — `./run_correctness.sh --operator <id>` and so on. Spelled out rather than left to be composed, because a consumer building the command line itself is a consumer who can build it wrong and get a silent whole-workset run.

reference.description: What **correctness** is judged against. Slow and obviously right. `kind: imported` is strongly preferred and the stage-3 half gives the argument in one line: a reference written from a reading of the kernel is how a correctness gate comes to agree with a bug. When the framework ships its own reference for this operator — and it usually does, in its own test suite — importing it means the gate is the one its authors wrote.

baseline.description: What **speedup** is judged against: the incumbent fast implementation, the thing actually running in the served engine today. Distinct from `reference`, and conflating the two is the single most common way a speedup number becomes meaningless — a 40x win over a naive fp32 loop is not a win over the tuned kernel it would replace. flashinfer-bench keeps them in separate fields for this reason and so does this.

edit_target.description: Where a consumer changes something. The unit is the framework-level entry function, not the device symbol.

source_owner.description: `aiter`, `sglang`, `triton`, … which checkout the file lives in.

repo_root_var.description: The placeholder the file paths are relative to, e.g. `${AITER_ROOT}`. A **variable and not a path**, because `handoff/locality.py` refuses the seal over a container-absolute root like `/sgl-workspace`; the expansion belongs in the environment, not in the artefact.

resolution_evidence.description: How it was established. Prose, and prose is right here: this is a *reason*, and M3.7.2's preference for yaml is over facts, not over arguments.

resolution_caveats.description: Stated uncertainties about facts the schema has no slot for. The stage-3 half's worked example is worth keeping in mind: the source file `operator_identity` declared for one kernel was **wrong**, and editing it would have changed a different kernel while every measurement continued to look plausible.

gates.description: What `run_correctness.sh` enforces. Every gate here is applied to every shape; a consumer's candidate passes only if the worst shape passes.

snr_db.description: Signal-to-noise against `reference`, in dB. 30 is the conventional figure and it is **weak at fp4** — necessarily so, where an element-wise tolerance is either meaningless or unsatisfiable. Passing it is not equivalence, and a workset over a low-precision operator should carry an additional gate below rather than raise this one.

extra.description: Operator-specific invariants, each a named predicate the driver evaluates. The stage-4 half carries the worked example and it is worth stating why it is not decoration: for a sampler softmax, 'every row sums to 1 within 1e-4' catches a wrong distribution that **no SNR threshold catches**, and the output feeds `torch.multinomial`.

provenance.description: Why this operator is in the workset at all, taken from m2's `profiling_evidence` rather than restated.

source.description: Which capture. Name the model and the phase — a decode capture of a different model is a legitimate source and a misleading one if the reader assumes otherwise.

magpie_row.description: M3.7.3 — 能通过工具标准化产出的尽量不自己搞：比如 magpie. **Magpie's own row, verbatim**, keys included: `Name`, `Calls`, `Self CUDA total (us)`, `Avg time (us)`, `% Total`, `Input Shapes`. Copied and not re-derived, so that a rename upstream shows up as a schema failure here rather than as a number that quietly means something else.

in_service_avg_us.description: Magpie's `Avg time (us)`, restated here under a name that says what it is: an average **inside the running service**, across mixed batch sizes and in contention with every other kernel. It is **not** the standalone baseline and the two can differ severalfold. The standalone number lives in `evidence/performance.json` and is the only one a speedup may be computed against. Keeping both, named differently, is cheaper than explaining the difference once and hoping.

forge.description: M3.7.6 — kernel forge well format one line script 作为额外项目, 在基础格式上封装. **An add-on layered over the base format, not a replacement for it.** Everything here is generated from `definition` + `workload` by `lib/forge_export.py`, and `check_workset_shape` re-runs that generation and diffs, so the two cannot drift. A consumer that does not use KernelForge ignores this block entirely and loses nothing: the base format carries the whole contract.

one_line.description: The one-line script. `--dry-run` prints the command it would run without running it, which is the flag that makes it reviewable.

driver.description: `scripts/forge_driver.py`, whose stdout contract forge-loop parses (`SNR: <x> dB`, `case_snr:`, `case_allclose:`, `time_ms:`/`case_ms:`) and which forge-loop treats as a **protected file** its optimising agent may not modify. That protection is exactly why `check_workset_runs` exists: forge-loop takes what this prints on trust, so something has to have run it first.

task.description: `forge_task.yaml` — the human-readable intent declaration KernelForge's own fellows emit.

cases.description: `tests/cases.json` — the `CASE_ID`-keyed export of `workload`, which is the form forge-loop's `--shape CASE_ID=<id>` selector needs.

generated_from.description: Which base documents this block is derived from. Declared so the regeneration check knows what to feed the exporter.

fellow.description: Which KernelForge fellow the kernel's language selects: `ck-fellow`, `triton-fellow`, …

notes.description: Prose, for reasons only. Anything here that is a *fact* belongs in a field above.

allOf.$comment: status and missing_fields are a biconditional, not two independent fields. The stage-3 half enforced this in validator code; it is mechanical, so it belongs here where the producer sees it too. `partial` with an empty list names no gap and `complete` with a non-empty one contradicts itself; both were reachable before this clause.

case_id.description: Stable, human-quotable, and the token both entrypoints and forge-loop's `--shape CASE_ID=<id>` select on.

uuid.description: The `workload.uuid` of the corresponding JSONL line. This is the join to the base format, and it is what makes `shapes` a *view* rather than a second source of truth.

axes.description: The `var` axes for this shape, exactly the `workload.axes` object of the matching line. Const axes are in the Definition and are not repeated.

role.description: What the shape is for. **At least one shape must include `performance`** — a workset every one of whose shapes is correctness-only cannot answer the question m4 is asked.

is_primary.description: Exactly one shape per operator carries this. It is the modal shape in the capture, and it is the one a single headline number refers to.

observed.description: True when this shape was seen in the profile; false when it was constructed to cover a tile boundary or an edge case. **A synthetic shape is legitimate and must be labelled**, because an operator optimised into a win on a shape the service never runs is a real and previously-made mistake.

observed_shapes.description: The raw tensor shapes as the profiler recorded them, when `observed`. The evidence behind `axes`, kept because `axes` is a *reading* of these and a reading can be wrong.

calls.description: How many times this shape occurred in the capture. The weight, when several shapes are reduced to one figure.

implementation.description: Either `reference` or `baseline`. `kind: imported` names an existing symbol; `kind: written` carries source and must say why importing was not possible.

path.description: For `kind: written`, the file inside the workset that holds it.

must_receive.description: Any pre-processing asymmetry between what the implementation is given and what the operator under test is given. The stage-3 half's worked example: the kernel gets shuffled weights, shuffled weight scales and sorted activation scales while the reference gets the unshuffled, unsorted originals. Getting this wrong produces a correctness gate that fails a correct kernel, which is the failure mode that wastes the most time.

report_environment.description: Enough of `environment.schema.json#/properties/fixed` to evaluate `ground_truth`'s two lists. A report that does not say where it was measured is not evidence.

correctness_report.$comment: Referenced as `workset.schema.json#/$defs/correctness_report`; the registry in assets/lib/schema.py resolves it without any change to that file.
correctness_report.description: What `run_correctness.sh --json` writes. **The same document shape whether `--impl` was given or not**, distinguished only by `impl`, so a consumer comparing its candidate against the baseline is comparing two instances of one format.

impl.description: `baseline` when `--impl` was absent. This field is the whole reason the format is shared.

passed.description: True iff every gate on every shape of every operator passed. Equal to `exit code == 0`, restated in the document so a reader holding only the JSON is not guessing.

failure.description: Non-null exactly when `ran` is false or `passed` is false. 'It did not run' and 'it ran and was wrong' are different facts and are never merged.

performance_report.$comment: Referenced as `workset.schema.json#/$defs/performance_report`. **This is m4's denominator** and the artefact M4.3.5 makes authoritative.
performance_report.description: What `run_performance.sh --json` writes. A speedup is `baseline.weighted_mean_ms / candidate.weighted_mean_ms` **per shape**, between two instances of this document produced by the same script on the same host. Aggregating across shapes before dividing hides an operator that got faster on the primary and slower on the other two.

correctness_report.description: Path to the correctness report for **this same impl**. A timing without a correctness result beside it is a measurement of an unknown function; `check_workset_runs` refuses a performance report whose companion did not pass.

weighted_mean_ms.description: Across shapes, weighted by `shapes[].calls`. A convenience; the per-shape figures are the record.

per_group_ms.description: One mean per group, each group a fresh process. Kept per-group and not only reduced, because `check_workset_runs` **recomputes** the weighted mean from these and rejects a record that disagrees with itself — a stored figure that does not follow from the raw numbers can only come from the record having been edited after it was measured.

rsd.description: Relative standard deviation across groups. The measured within-arm round-to-round spread on a steady node is ~2%; `check_workset_runs` fails above `max_rsd` (default 0.10) because a noisy baseline is worse than no baseline — the first candidate that lands on a fast sample looks like a win and the campaign chases noise for hours.
